article_content: 'The Taliban government of Afghanistan has requested membership in China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and plans to send a technical team to Beijing for negotiations. Kabul recently sent a delegation to the Belt and Road Forum, which concluded on Wednesday. Afghanistan was among 35 countries that signed an agreement on digital economy and green development. Commerce Minister Haji Nooruddin Azizi stated, 'We requested China to allow us to join the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor and BRI.' The corridor is a key part of BRI, China's major infrastructure project in Asia, aiming to boost trade and commerce. An Afghan technical team will visit China to address remaining obstacles, though Azizi didn't provide further details. He emphasized, 'China should invest in Afghanistan, as we offer resources like lithium, copper, and iron. Afghanistan is now more than ever ready for investment.' Chinese companies, including the Metallurgical Corp. of China Ltd (MCC), are already active in Afghanistan, primarily in mineral extraction. MCC is negotiating a major copper mine project with the Taliban, supported by Azizi. Talks have faced delays due to the mine's location near historical sites. China appointed a new ambassador to Kabul last month, being the first country to do so after the Taliban takeover in August 2021. The previous US-backed government collapsed without resistance before the last American troops left. The US has frozen $7 billion in Afghan central bank funds at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with additional funds frozen in other countries.'

Afganistan oli üks 35 riigist, mis allkirjastasid digitaalmajanduse ja rohealase arengu lepingu. Kaubandusminister Haji Nooruddin Azizi ütles: 'Me palusime Hiinal lubada meil osaleda Hiina-Pakistani Majanduskoridoris ja BRI-s.' Koridor on oluline osa BRI-st, Hiina suurest infrastruktuuriprojektist Aasias, mille eesmärk on edendada kaubandust ja majandust. Afganistani tehniline meeskond läheb Hiinasse, et lahendada jäänud takistusi, kuid Azizi ei andnud täpsemaid detaile. Ta rõhutas: 'Hiina peaks Afganistanis investeerima, sest meil on kõige olulikumad ressursid nagu liitium, copper ja iron. Afganistan on nüüd rohkem kui kunagi varem valmis investeeringuteks.' Hiina firmade hulgas, eriti Metallurgia Korporatsioon Hiina Ltd (MCC), on juba Afganistanis tegev mineraalide kaevandamisega. MCC läbiräägib Talibaniga suure kuprarikka projekti, mida Azizi toetab. Eelmine Ameerika Ühendriikide toetatud valitsus varises kokku vastupanuta enne viimaste Ameerika sõjaväelaste lahkumist. Ameerika Ühendriigid on külmakanud 7 miljardi dollarit Afganistani keskpanki fondisid Federal Reserve Bank of New Yorkis hoitud, koos lisafondidega teistes riikides.'

article_content: JUBA - South Sudan's largest hospital has halted operations due to a mysterious fuel shortage, allegedly orchestrated by government officials for personal gain. Doctors at Juba Teaching Hospital revealed that emergency operations have ceased, leading to multiple patient deaths, mirroring the tragic events of January. A doctor, requesting anonymity, disclosed that patients are now forced to purchase fuel for surgeries or seek private clinics, an impossibility for the hospital's impoverished patients. A pregnant woman in labor suffered epileptic seizures while her family sought fuel for a C-section, highlighting the dire situation. Fuel prices have skyrocketed, with black market rates unreachable, as the economy collapses under the transitional government's watch. Citizens accuse officials of hoarding fuel, worsening the crisis. Motorbike queues for fuel reflect the broader shortages. The hospital barely functions at night, leaving victims of accidents and violence without aid. Families struggle to afford fuel for urgent surgeries, further straining the healthcare system. The petroleum minister remains unavailable, fueling suspicions of corruption. With no refineries, South Sudan imports fuel, worsening dependency and enabling corruption.

article_content: NATO and the European Union have condemned recent peaceful protests by ethnic Serbs in northern Kosovo, as Serbia faces pressure to end the unrest in the tense border region. In a statement Thursday, NATO's governing body expressed concern about continuing tensions in northern Kosovo, calling violence against peacekeepers 'unacceptable.' Minor injuries have occurred during clashes between NATO soldiers and Serb protestors. Since July, Serbs in the Kosovo-Serbia border region have set up symbolic barricades after Kosovo's ethnic Albanian government attempted to control the border area under de-facto Serb rule. NATO welcomed Serbian President Boris Tadic's call to remove barricades, but emphasized the need for constructive dialogue. Violence flared Monday when Serbs reportedly fired on peacekeeping forces during attempts to remove blockades, with peacekeepers using rubber bullets, water cannons, and tear gas. NATO commanders stated they will use lethal force if necessary to protect troops, while Tadic urged peacekeepers to halt forcible removal of roadblocks. EU foreign ministers in Brussels condemned the violence during their meeting Thursday, as Serbia and Kosovo representatives held EU-brokered peace talks. EU officials reiterated that Serbia must resolve the impasse for its EU candidacy bid. The Serbs' blockades restrict NATO access to a military base, but dialogue continues. NATO demands unrestricted movement in Kosovo. Ethnic Serbs remain opposed to Kosovo's 2008 independence declaration. Some information for this report was provided by AP, AFP, and Reuters.

article_content: 'CAIRO - Egyptian authorities are enhancing internet security as President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi promotes international investment, amid claims of misinformation about the Red Sea islands agreement with Saudi Arabia. Since late May, certain websites and VPN services have been restricted, reportedly to combat illegal activities. The Association for Freedom of Thought and Expression claims 64 websites are now blocked. Among them is Yanair Gate, which published critical articles, including those about opposition to the islands deal and quotes from a rights lawyer potential presidential candidate. The government maintains the islands were always Saudi territory. El-Sissi has focused on security since 2013. Recent blocks include Al-Jazeera and sites linked to banned groups like the Muslim Brotherhood and Hamas. VPN services like Tunnelbear, used to bypass restrictions, have also been targeted. During his visit to Germany, El-Sissi aimed to boost economic ties, but civil society groups face challenges under a new NGO law. Rights lawyer Khaled Ali, opposing the islands deal, faces legal challenges. International groups have criticized Egypt's internet policies.'
translated_content: 'CAIRO - Egipti võimud parandavad internetiturvalust, kui president Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi edendab rahvusvahelist investeeringut, vaatamata väidetele, et levitatakse ebauske aktuaalseid teemasid punelaiuku saarte üleandmise kohta Saudi Araabiale. Alates maikuu lõpust on piiratud teatud veebisaite ja VPN-teenuseid, peaegu kahjulike tegevuste vastu võitlemise eesmärgil. Mõtte- ja väljendusvabaduse assotsiatsioon väidab, et 64 veebisaiti on nüüd blokeeritud. Nende hulgas on Yanair Gate, mis avaldas kriitilisi artikleid, sealhulgas vastupanikut saarete üleandmisele ja viiteid õiguskysimustega seotud kandidaadile. Valitsus väidab, et saared kuulusid alati Saudi Araabiale. El-Sissi on keskendunud julgeolekule alates 2013. aastast. Hiljutised blokeerimised hulka on kuulunud Al-Jazeera ja veebisaite, mis on seotud keelatud rühmitustega nagu Muslimi Venemaa ja Hamas. VPN-teenused nagu Tunnelbear, mis kasutatakse piirangute üleelamiseks, on samuti sihtidestiks. El-Sissi Saksamaa visiidil püüdis ta edendada majandussidemeid, kuid ühiskonnaorganisatsioonidel on raskusi uue NGO seadusega. Õigusadvokaat Khaled Ali, kes vastustab saarete üleandmist, näeb silm Ringsi õiguslikke probleeme. Rahvusvahelised grupid on kritiseerinud Egiptuse internetipolicite.'
